title: Function Health Lab Failure Rate
dataSources: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body composition (`bodycomp:measure`), blood pressure (`bloodpressure:reading`).
app: Biohacking data — HRV straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=function:lab
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(lab_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by marker_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Function Health lab records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each marker.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize lab_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per marker.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It rates which parts of your Function Health lab data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
